title: Strix now supports Vercel AI Gateway
description: Strix , the open-source AI penetration testing tool, can now run on any of the 400+ models on Vercel AI Gateway . Strix can reach models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Kimi, GLM, Deepseek, and others through a single API with no markup, removing the need to sign up for multiple providers. Usage and cost are tracked across all models in AI Gateway. Strix selects the Gateway through STRIX_LLM , where the model is the standard AI Gateway <provider>/<model> ID behind a vercel_ai_gateway/ prefix: See Strix's AI Gateway setup guide to configure it and get started today. title: IP geolocation now covers more visitors at higher resolution
description: IP geolocation on Vercel now resolves visitor locations with finer network granularity, delivering city-level data for nearly all requests and postal-code data for 90% of traffic. Geolocation data is now refreshed more often, so locations keep up as IP ranges are reassigned and routing changes. This is enabled for all projects with no code or configuration changes required. Existing geolocation headers along with the geolocation() helper in @vercel/functions , return the same fields for Vercel Functions and Routing Middleware . If you use geolocation for access controls, localization, or compliance, some visitors will now resolve to a different city or country, most often traffic from VPNs, hosting providers, and leased IP ranges: Physical termination location: Subnets announced from a hosting provider in a different country than their regional internet registry (RIR) record now resolve to the data center where the traffic actually terminates. Testing geo-dependent routes: Verify access rules against an IP's active network location rather than its static registry allocation. Read the request headers documentation for all available geolocation headers and fields. Read more
